previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of multiple strokes, tracheostomy, GJ tube, atrial fibrillation, and recent UTI was admitted for fever and blood from his G-tube, initially brought in for routine replacement. Imaging showed no abdominal leak, but chest findings revealed bilateral lower lobe infiltrates concerning for hospital-associated pneumonia. He was treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics, and a mini-BAL identified Serratia marcescens and Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Antibiotics were narrowed to levofloxacin, which he continued via G-tube. The G-tube was successfully replaced without complications. His white count improved, fever resolved, and he remained stable. C. diff was ruled out despite history. His atrial fibrillation was managed with warfarin, temporarily supported with heparin until therapeutic INR was achieved. A stage 2 sacral pressure ulcer was monitored with wound care. He was discharged to extended care on oral levofloxacin for a full 14-day course and with warfarin dose increased to 4mg daily, to be titrated by rehab based on INR.

radiology_notes.text:
PROCEDURE: Replacement of 14 ___ ___ gastrojejunal feeding tube. 
  
HISTORY: ___ year old man with CVAs and long standing GJ tube that fell out. 
  
ANESTHESIA: 10 mL of viscous lidocaine was administered around the 
gastrostomy tract. No intravenous sedation or injected lidocaine was 
required. 
  
PHYSICIANS: Dr. ___ and Dr ___ performed the procedure. Dr.
___ attending radiologist, supervised the procedure. 
  
PROCEDURE AND FINDINGS: Informed consent was obtained outlining the risks and
benefits of the procedure involved. Following this, the patient was brought to
the angiography suite and placed supine on the imaging table. The upper
abdomen was prepped and draped in the usual sterile 
fashion. A preprocedure huddle and timeout were performed as per ___ 
protocol. 
  
A scout fluoroscopic image did not show residual catheter. ___ ___  catheter
was placed through the existing tract into the stomach. Injection of contrast
confirmed the tip of the catheter to lie in the stoamch. the catheter was
successfully manipulated to the jejunum with an aid of 0.035 ___ wire. Of
note, patient has partial malrotation with midline locations of ligament of
Treitz.  Over the ___ wire, a new 14 ___ ___ gastrojejunal feeding
tube was advanced. The pigtail formed within the duodenum, in a post-pyloric
position. The patient tolerated the procedure well. There were no early
complications. The catheter was secured with a Stat lock and sterile dressings
were applied. 
  
IMPRESSION: 
1. Uncomplicated replacement of 14 ___ ___ gastrojejunal feeding tube. 
The catheter may be used for feeding immediately. 
2. Of note, patient has partial congenital malrotation with midline locations
of ligament of Treitz.
